A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HiVE-MIL research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, revised and added content.

before.justification: v1 reports original few-shot classification experiments on three TCGA datasets, alongside ablations, alignment measurements and computational analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds Camelyon16 results, further comparisons, prompt-validation measurements and expanded computational evaluations.

M1.justification: The hierarchy, TGDF, GraphSAGE/MSA aggregation, HTCL and default top-k inference remain. The expanded message-passing description and term-plus-explanation prompt instruction document existing behavior; the corrected logit equation does not establish a changed implementation.

E1.justification: v4 retains all three TCGA datasets and adds Camelyon16 evaluation using CONCH in the 16-shot setting (Appendix K, Table 8). This is a bounded extension beyond TCGA within few-shot WSI classification.

E2.justification: v4 broadens comparison to a slide-level foundation model, MADELEINE with linear probing (Table 9), and adds MLP/MLP and attention/attention interaction controls (Table 13). The main MIL comparator set remains unchanged. TransMIL is removed specifically from the computational-efficiency comparison.

E3.justification: v4 introduces LLM-judge and CONCH-similarity validation protocols. The TGDF sweep replaces alpha=0.1 with negative thresholds and a no-TGDF control, and adds filtered-pair ratios while dropping ACC/AUC reporting there. Computational testing changes from one WSI with 955/13,929 patches to two with 1,880/28,249 and 2,633/40,777 patches, adding peak GPU memory. Core TCGA splits and training defaults remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds tests of description class-discriminativeness and semantic consistency, while Appendix M.4 tests replacing graph interactions with MLP/attention modules. TGDF threshold analysis and computational scalability testing are expanded. The text-format, LLM-choice, HTCL, scale and top-k studies already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five repeated random splits/runs and report means with standard deviations. The new checklist reiterates this practice; no increased repeat count, confidence-interval procedure or significance test is reported.

E6.justification: Table 1, Tables 2–3 and most matched appendix tables retain their values. v4 adds prompt-validation, MADELEINE and interaction-control results; its new Camelyon16 comparison reports macro F1 of 93.22±5.06 for HiVE-MIL versus 91.97±5.22 for ViLa-MIL. Computational results are replaced under different slide conditions. For retained QuiltNet alpha=0, BRCA macro F1 changes from 75.97±3.41 to 76.00±3.47 (v1 Table 7; v4 Table 15).

T1.justification: Equation 7 replaces an ambiguous expression normalized by the number of classes with an explicit per-class average over class-specific text prompts after per-prompt top-k patch aggregation. This corrects the mathematical specification of the logits. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same method scope and performance claims. The introduction narrows its criticism of prior methods from lacking explicit same-scale modality interactions to insufficient interaction modeling and relational inductive bias.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive explanations of semantic versus spatial connectivity, graph inductive bias and prompt semantic reliability (Appendices G, M.4 and B). It explains performance loss from aggressive filtering, explicitly discusses dataset/backbone transfer limitations, and replaces the earlier optimal-efficiency-balance interpretation with scalability measurements and planned parallelization.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly documents HeteroConv, relation-specific transformations, feature concatenation and ReLU; the prompt template explicitly requests terms with visual explanations. Existing hyperparameters, hardware and code/split access information are retained. However, the replacement efficiency section omits v1's explicit PLIP/16-shot qualifier.

R1.justification: Five references are added concerning graph inductive biases, Camelyon16, LLM-as-a-judge and MADELEINE. They support refined prior-method criticism and positioning against slide-level foundation models. The established MIL/VLM related-work discussion is largely retained.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the principal section sequence remain intact, with localized revisions to prediction, TGDF, prior-work criticism and limitations. Appendix topics are reordered, ablations and hyperparameter sensitivity are separated, and a NeurIPS checklist and acknowledgments are added.

P2.justification: v4 adds tables for prompt validation, Camelyon16, MADELEINE and interaction controls, restructures the threshold-sensitivity table, and replaces v1's efficiency bubble plot (Figure 9) with a two-slide resource table (Table 17). Existing main figures and tables are also repositioned and resized; most earlier figures are retained.

improvement.justification: Camelyon16 evaluation, the MADELEINE comparison and direct graph-replacement controls address important gaps in v1's evidence for generalization and architectural choices. Corrected logit specification and explicit memory/scalability measurements further improve assessability. These gains substantially strengthen the paper despite remaining weaknesses: prompt validation is still proxy-based, and new Table 5 contains inconsistent counts, including 21 (8/23), which limit confidence in that analysis.
